title: Fischer's band and prizefight advertising parades
summary: Street bands advertising fights, drinks in bars, and the claim that alcohol stunted his growth.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Yeah, you worked it right. Do you remember Fischer's band?

Oh yeah, he was a pretty good client at that time. Fischer and George Schilling played trombone. Well I've talked to Hal Schilling. And there was Diddy Stevens, and there was Darren Hughes, and there was a patch over his eye. We used to play the Advertiser Fights, and walk around the streets and we had a fight on there, and Kit Costner used to play trombone. The night he was fighting he'd come play and watch the street with us, the night before he was going in the fight. He was going in the fight.
He must have been a tough guy.

And they used to stop on the corner in the bar rooms, you know, you'd play a couple of numbers and get you in and have a drink. They used to sit me on the bar and save me booze. That's what stunned my growth. I should be six foot something. Oh I don't know.
That would have made a difference. Yeah they say alcohol stunned your growth. I was young then.
Merritt isn't much taller than you. Merritt isn't much taller than you. No.
I said to Merritt, I said, holy or not Merritt, he says, 62. He says, that's not my age, that's the weather temperature I'd say.
